about: Where the readings of a Sunday or major feast meet in the Bible's own cross-references, and a Father's comment on the Gospel. Built by scripts/launch/make-readings-together.ts.

sources.xrefs: OpenBible.info cross references (CC BY 4.0); votes are community relevance scores, not Church teaching
sources.quoted: The app's own notes on New Testament quotations of the Old (public/data/lens/quotes.json)

2028-01-01.title: Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God (The Octave Day of the Nativity of the Lord)

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: As men who were truly watching, they said not, Let us see (the child; but) the word which has come to pass, i.e. the Word which was from the beginning, let us see how it has been made flesh for us, since this very Word is the Lord. For it follows, Which the Lord has made, and has shown to us; i.e. Let us see how the Lord has made Himself, and has shown His flesh to us.

quote.author: Leo the Great
quote.label: Leo
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Thou art troubled, Herod, without cause. Thy nature cannot contain Christ, nor is the Lord of the world content with the narrow bounds of thy dominion. He, whom thou wouldest not should reign in Judaea, reigns every where.

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord having overcome the tempter, power was added to Him, i.e. as far as regards the manifestation of it. Hence it is said, And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The fourth miracle after Jesus came to Capernaum was the healing of a leprous man. But since He illumined the fourth day with the sun, and made it more glorious than the rest, we ought to think this work more glorious than those that went before; of which it is said, And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Our Lord did not baptize with the baptism wherewith He had been baptized; for He was baptized by a servant, as a lesson of humility to us, and in order to bring us to the Lord’s baptism, i.e. His own; for Jesus baptized, as the Lord, the Son of God.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: In a matter which has been related by others Luke has rightly given us only a summary, and has left more to be understood than expressed in the fact, that our Lord was baptized by John. As it is said, Now when all were baptized, it came to pass.

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord having overcome the tempter, power was added to Him, i.e. as far as regards the manifestation of it. Hence it is said, And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit.

quote.author: Cyril of Alexandria
quote.label: Cyril
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: But what prevents Him from filling men with awe, though He were the Son as was supposed of Joseph? Do you not see the divine miracles, Satan already prostrate, men released from their sickness?

2028-02-02.title: Feast of the Presentation of the Lord

quote.author: Cyril of Alexandria
quote.label: Cyril
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Having sufficiently taught the people, He returns again to His mighty works, and by the employment of fishing fishes for His disciples. Hence it follows, When he had left off speaking, he said to Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: But being about to utter His divine oracles, He begins to rise higher; although He stood in a low place, yet as it is said, He lifted up his eyes. What is lifting up the eyes, but to disclose a more hidden light?

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Having spoken above of what they might suffer from their enemies, He now points out how they ought to conduct themselves towards their enemies’ saying, But I say to you who hear.

quote.author: Cyril of Alexandria
quote.label: Cyril
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord added to what had gone before a very necessary parable, as it is said, And he spoke a parable to them, for His disciples were the future teachers of the world, and it therefore became them to know the way of a virtuous life, having their minds illuminated as it were by a divine brightness, that they should not be blind leaders of the blind.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The next weapon he uses is that of boasting, which always causes the offender to fall down; for they who love to boast of the glory of their virtue descend from the stand and vantage ground of their good deeds. Hence it is said, And he led him to Jerusalem.

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: While Christ is engaged in prayer, Peter is heavy with sleep, for he was weak, and did what was natural to man; as it is said, But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep. But when they awake, they behold His glory, and the two men with Him; as it follows, And when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

2028-03-20.title: Solemnity of Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: This passage is objected to us by the Emperor Julian in his Discrepancy of the Evangelists. Matthew calls Joseph the son of Jacob, Luke makes him the son of Heli. He did not know the Scripture manner, one was his father by nature, the other by law.

2028-03-25.title: Solemnity of the Annunciation of the Lord

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: But all are not as Mary, that when they conceive the word of the Holy Spirit, they bring forth; for some put forth the word prematurely, others have Christ in the womb, but not yet formed.

2028-04-09.title: Palm Sunday of the Passion on the Lord

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Luke returns to those things which were going on before the governor, from which he had digressed in order to relate what took place with Herod; saying as follows, And Pilate, when he had called, yet from which we infer, that he has omitted the part wherein Pilate questioned our Lord what He had to answer to His accusers.

2028-04-14.title: Friday of the Passion of the Lord (Good Friday)

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: It was a band not of Jews, but of soldiers, granted, we must understand, by the Governor, with legal authority to take the criminal, as He was considered, and crush any opposition that might be made.

2028-04-15.title: Holy Saturday At the Easter Vigil in the Holy Night of Easter

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Now this place has caused great perplexity to many, because while St. Luke says, Very early in the morning, Matthew says that it was in the evening of the sabbath that the women came to the sepulcher. But you may suppose that the Evangelists spoke of different occasions, so as to understand both different parties of women, and different appearances.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Mary Magdalene, undoubtedly the most fervent in love, of all the women that ministered to our Lord; so that John deservedly mentions her only, and says nothing of the others who were with her, as we know from the other Evangelists.

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Or because He waited till all were assembled: and with shut doors, that he might show how that in the very same way he had risen again, i.e. with the stone lying on the sepulcher.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The preceding words of the Evangelist seem to indicate the end of the book, but He goes on farther to give an account of our Lord’s appearance by the sea of Tiberias: After these things Jesus showed Himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication. Encænia is the feast of the dedication of the temple; from the Greek word signifying new. The dedication of any thing new was called encænia.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: After He had said, And shall straightway glorify Him, that they might not think that God was going to glorify Him in such a way, as that He would no longer have any converse with them on earth, He says, Little children, yet a little while I am with you: as if He said, I shall indeed straightway be glorified by My resurrection, but I shall not straightway ascend to heaven.
